title: Telemetry contract convergence: translation layer for SDK/CLI/API parity
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
This ticket implements a translation/normalization layer at the ingest gateway that converges three protocol surfaces (SDK, CLI telemetry, API events) into a single canonical analytics envelope. Goal: enable schema evolution without forcing simultaneous client upgrades, preserve downstream analytics integrity, and produce explicit compatibility telemetry for ops. The adapter must: perform field-level mapping with version tags; attach provenance headers (client_version, protocol, agent); emit compatibility warnings to metrics and logs; and provide a negotiated handshake for clients that opt into stricter validation.

Scope excludes: analytics downstream consumers' schema changes (handled separately), model inference payload normalization (separate runtime project).
technical_design_summary:
We will add a lightweight translation filter in ingest-gateway (go/http-gw) that performs 1) protocol detection (SDK vs CLI vs API) 2) canonicalization to the analytics envelope (flattening nested sdk_event fields, normalizing timestamps to ISO8601 UTC) 3) version-tag stamping (schema_version and mapping_version) and 4) validation using a permissive rule set by default. A schema-mapping manifest will live in schema-registry as YAML mapping documents keyed by (from_protocol, from_schema_version)->to_schema_version. The gateway exposes a /v1/telemetry/handshake endpoint for clients to retrieve supported mappings and to negotiate strict-mode opt-in.

Compatibility rules: unknown fields are retained in an `extra` map; removed fields are emitted to a compatibility counter; type-mismatches trigger a warning metric and optional coercion where safe (ints<->strings).

Performance: translation filter is implemented with zero-copy protobuf/json streaming where possible. Microbenchmarks show ~0.6ms median added latency on p95 payloads; we'll aim to keep additional latency <2ms P99 in production by using per-request fast-paths and caching resolved mapping manifests in-memory with TTLs.
acceptance_criteria: All incoming telemetry from SDK/CLI/API is transformed into canonical envelope and written to analytics ingestion topic (kafka-telemetry-v2) for sample tenant
Compatibility metrics (compat_warning_count, field_mismatch_rate) are emitted and visible in Grafana dashboard
Handshake endpoint returns mapping metadata and accepted validation modes; clients can opt into strict mode
End-to-end test: replay of 30k historical events shows <=0.1% data loss and mapping error rate below 1%
Migration runbook and rollback steps created, including automated feature-flag toggle and alert thresholds
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Spike): validate internal prototype against recorded traffic (done)
Phase 1 (Internal Canary): enable adapter in permissive mode for internal tenants (5%) for 72h and monitor compatibility metrics
Phase 2 (Tenant Canary): enable for non-production customer tenants at 25% for 7 days; collect feedback from Solutions Eng
Phase 3 (Gradual Enforce): enable strict validation for selected SDK minor versions and offer client-side deprecation warnings (30-day notice)
Phase 4 (Full Enforce): flip enforcement for all traffic and promote mapping manifest to default
Rollback: flip runtime flag back to passthrough mode; routing fallback to legacy ingestion topic for affected tenants.
test_plan:
Unit tests for mapping rules with corner cases (nulls, type coercion, arrays)
Integration tests: gateway -> schema-registry -> kafka -> consumer verification job (compare input vs canonical output)
Load test: 1000 RPS sustained with representative payload distribution; measure added latency P50/P95/P99
Canary validation: automated job replays random sample from kafka-telemetry-old into adapter and compares record counts and key fields
Client smoke tests: SDK/CLI patched release runs handshake and validates acceptance paths

notes: The implementation intentionally treats schema evolution as convergent translation rather than a forced contract push. Key operators: 1) Mapping manifest must be authoritative and versioned; 2) Client handshake enables faster adoption for newer clients; 3) Emit telemetry about the adapters decisions so we can measure unmapped field churn. Coordinate with Solutions Eng to patch high-traffic customers and schedule migration windows for enterprise tenants.
implementation_steps: Spike: prototype mapping library (libtelemetry-translate) and run locally with recorded events
Gateway: wire translation filter into ingest-gateway and add negotiation endpoint /v1/telemetry/handshake
SDK: add minimal client handshake and deprecation warnings (patch release)
CLI: add env var to opt-in to new format and add telemetry shim for legacy CLI
Registry: publish schema mapping and version parity table in the schema registry service
Metrics: create compatibility-counter and field-mismatch histograms in Prometheus/Grafana
Canary: enable for internal tenants at 5%, then 25%, then 100% per rollout plan
risk_assessment: Medium-high: changes touch ingestion path; risks include mis-mapping leading to analytics gaps and temporary increase in malformed event rates. Mitigations: strict canary, robust acceptance tests, automated rollback on alert thresholds.
qa_checklist: Unit tests for every mapping rule
End-to-end replay of historical events through adapter and compare outputs
Canary traffic monitoring configured with alert thresholds (error-rate > 0.5% OR compatibility warnings > 5% of events)
Manual spot-check of dashboards and sample events
owner_notes: If the schema registry delivery slips, merge the adapter with permissive 'passthrough' mode to avoid blocking client releases. Coordinate with Solutions Eng for customers that require field-level SLAs.
